correctness.rationale: The geometric blow-up model gives exactly 16 (-1)-curves and 40 ordinary double nodes; a Hamming-distance-four model reproduces all intersections and excludes triple nodes. The normalization/conductor identity explicitly accounts for 80 branches, including rational nodes with conjugate branches. Picard Frobenius trace and these conductor counts prove the formula for all finite fields/extension degrees. An exhaustive 1920-element signed-permutation check generates 18 types and verifies the first-extension table and distinct symbolic zeta profiles. A finite-field F9 arc verifies existence of the unique new nonsplit q=3 zero case; five F5 conic points give the already-known split case. Independent external verification is not asserted.

originality.rationale: The split q=5 result is known from Hirschfeld (Knecht–Reyes §1) and excluded; complete-surface zeta is covered by Rybakov and Banwait–Fité–Loughran, and classical 16-line incidences are known. The assessed new statement is the explicit 18-form exceptional-boundary zeta and the nonsplit F3 full quartic constructed from a 1+2+2 arc. Source comparisons concern implications, not title matching, and no inspected source states these open-boundary results. Historical priority remains provisional, especially for old full-surface tables and specialist moduli literature.

value.rationale: The natural complete exceptional divisor is the canonical union of all (-1)-curves on a smooth quartic del Pezzo. Its complement is also a very-stable locus in related moduli geometry. The all-forms zeta arithmetic determines an exact invariant across every Frobenius conjugacy class; the unexpected nonsplit F3 all-rational-points-on-boundary example closes the full-surface existence question beyond the classical split classification. Both are structural, motivated results rather than arbitrary slices or merely recomputing 16 intersections.
